items.title: Discover, Explore & Get Inspired - VIP+ Showcase Day | November 26 | 12 to 4 PM | FCC - Byblos Campus.
items.body:
Dear Students,

What can you create when creativity meets innovation and teamwork?

Join us for VIP+ Showcase Day, organized by the School of Engineering, and discover what your fellow students have been working on!

With 18 VIP+ teams showcasing their projects, this is your opportunity to:

- Explore innovative projects and creative ideas developed by LAU students.
- Get inspired by what students from different disciplines can achieve through teamwork.
- Discover VIP+ and learn how you can participate in future projects.
- Connect with fellow students, exchange ideas, and explore opportunities beyond the classroom.

Students from all majors and disciplines are welcome.

Event Details:

- Date: Thursday, November 26, 2026
- Time: 12:00 PM – 4:00 PM
- Venue: Frem Multipurpose Room, Byblos Campus

Come curious, leave inspired, and discover what you could be part of next!

We look forward to seeing you there!

VIP+ Team

items.title: Recognizing students’ global leadership: Millennium Fellowship
items.body:
Dear Students,

The United Nations Academic Impact and Millennium Campus Network (MCN) proudly present the
Millennium Fellowship.

The program convenes, challenges and celebrates bold undergraduate students advancing the
Sustainable Development Goals on campus and in communities. As a Millennium Fellow, you will hone your skills, take concrete action and earn recognition. There is no cost for selected students.

Undergraduate students can apply by the next priority deadline:
November 30, 2026. The class of 2027 will run from August to December 2027.

items.title: SOE Research Track Certificate of Completion
items.body:
Dear SOE Students,

As you prepare your Spring 2027 course schedule, we invite you to consider pursuing the
Research Track and earning its Certificate of Completion. The track is designed for undergraduate students who want to go beyond the traditional curriculum through meaningful faculty-supervised research.

To qualify for the certificate, students must complete:

-
6 credits of Undergraduate Research Experience (URE).
-
The 3-credit course GNE598 Research Methods for Engineers.

GNE598 will be offered in Spring 2027. Students may enroll once they have completed 3 credits of URE or are concurrently registered in 3 credits of URE. The course builds core research skills, including conducting a literature review, formulating research
 questions, practicing research ethically, and writing proposals and research papers.

Why join the Research Track?

-
Hands-on experience working closely with faculty on real research problems.

-
A formal certificate that documents your research training and sets your profile apart.

-
Stronger applications for graduate programs and fast-track PhD pathways.
-
A competitive edge for fellowships, scholarships and R&D careers.

Further information is available at Research Track Certificate of Completion. For inquiries, feel free to contact the SOE Dean’s Office at (dean.soe@lau.edu.lb).

items.body:

Pause Before You Puff. Your health, your choice!
